items.title: Lemon Nash Interview, 1961-06-20
items.q: He came up the time of Fester Monette over in Algea... All those guys were great violin players, you know.

ctx.x: That was Cornelius. No, no, that's George Jones who played the bass violin. You're right, Cornelius played the violin. That's right, he died. Yeah, he was a good violin player. He came up the time of Fester Monette over in Algea, across the river. All those guys were great violin players, you know. Fester Monette, Cornelius, and Fester Clayborne William out of Donisonville. They came there once and won the contest. Yeah, they won the contest here playing once. They had a very, very good band. And then, all the…
Did you have Buddy Bolin in your shop?

Well, I used to fool around a musician, they taught me a few things. Fester Monette crossed the river. And I used to be with one of the best guitar players in town, they called him Frank Wagner. He hung himself. He was working on the P.W.A., things got rough around there and he couldn't support his mother like he wanted, so he just tied a rope around his neck. And he got, stood on a box, tied a rope around his neck and kicked the box from under him. And he fell on his neck and hung himself right uptown there. He…
